How long does a kitchen remodel take?
The whole process (planning, designing, ordering, scheduling, installing) can take anywhere from 3-6 months. Much of that time is invested before the actual work begins. A Custom Tile Bathroom Renovation for the Reap Family in Harpers Ferry, WV

Oct 14, 2026

When the Reap family was ready to update the bathrooms in their Harpers Ferry home, they came to Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths for a project that would cover three spaces at once: the master bath, the guest bath, and the powder room. The scope called for custom tile work throughout, Schluter waterproofing systems in both full bathrooms, and heated floors in the master suite. Every element was selected and installed with long-term durability in mind.

Heated Floors and a Custom Tile Shower

The master bathroom received the most comprehensive treatment of the three spaces. The shower was built on a 72″ x 72″ Schluter shower pan with a curbless entry, and the walls were prepped with Kerdi waterproofing membrane before tile installation began. Le Dolomiti White 12×24 tile was installed throughout in a brick pattern, running from the shower floor up the walls to the full 120″ ceiling height. Brushed nickel Schluter edging frames the tile cleanly, and two tiled shower niches — each with a 2×2 mosaic accent in the back — add both function and detail to the design.

The bathroom floor received the same Le Dolomiti White tile in a brick pattern, installed over Schluter Ditra-Heat electric floor heating underlayment. The heating system was tested to manufacturer specifications during installation and carries a 10-year manufacturer warranty. Laticrete Spectralok1 grout in Frosty was used throughout for a consistent, clean finish.

Custom Shower and Coordinated Tile

The guest bath follows the same design language as the master, maintaining a cohesive look across the home. The shower was built on a 44″ x 61″ Schluter shower pan with a tile curb, and the walls were waterproofed with Kerdi membrane before tile installation. Le Dolomiti White 12×24 tile was installed in a brick pattern on both the shower floor and walls, again running to 120″ ceiling height with brushed nickel Schluter edging. A single tiled niche with a 2×2 mosaic accent provides built-in storage in the shower.

The bathroom floor received the same 12×24 tile in a brick pattern, installed over Schluter Ditra uncoupling underlayment. Laticrete Spectralok1 grout in Frosty ties the finishes together with the master bath.

Consistent Finishes Throughout

The powder room received 12×24 Le Dolomiti White tile in a brick pattern, installed over Schluter Ditra uncoupling underlayment with Spectralok1 grout in Frosty. A brushed nickel Schluter transition strip provides a finished edge where the tile meets the adjoining floor. The result keeps all three spaces connected by the same material palette, giving the home a unified feel from room to room.

Waterproofing, Materials, and Craftsmanship

Every wet area in this project was built on the Schluter system, which integrates the shower pan, Kerdi waterproofing membrane, and tile installation into a single, fully warranted system:

Schluter shower pans and Kerdi membrane carry a lifetime warranty to the original homeowner
Ditra-Heat electric floor heating in the master bath carries a 10-year manufacturer warranty
Schluter Ditra uncoupling membrane in the guest bath and powder room, also lifetime warranted
Le Dolomiti White 12×24 tile used consistently across all three spaces
Laticrete Spectralok1 grout in Frosty throughout
Brushed nickel Schluter edging and transitions for a finished, polished look

Mountaineer’s tile team handled every aspect of this project in-house, from waterproofing and underlayment to the final grout and edging. The attention to detail in a multi-room tile project like this one is what separates a renovation that holds up over time from one that doesn’t.

Three Rooms, One Cohesive Renovation

The Reap bathroom renovation is a strong example of what Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths delivers when a project spans multiple spaces. With consistent materials, professional-grade waterproofing systems, and tile work carried out by an experienced in-house team, all three bathrooms now feel like they belong together — and are built to last for the life of the home.

A Fresh Kitchen Renovation for the Petrasek Family in Martinsburg, WV

Aug 5, 2026

When the Petrasek family was ready to transform their Martinsburg kitchen, they turned to Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths for a renovation that would bring both style and function to the heart of the home. The project involved a full cabinet replacement, new quartz countertops, updated electrical and plumbing, and a fresh coat of paint throughout the kitchen and living room. From start to finish, Mountaineer’s in-house team handled every detail.

Layout and Structural Work

The existing pantry door, frame, and trim were removed to reconfigure the space and make way for the new cabinet design. The existing base and wall cabinets were carefully removed and retained by the homeowners. Plumbing was revised to accommodate the new propane stove location, and new venthood ducting with an exterior cap was installed for proper kitchen ventilation. New drywall was patched and installed as needed throughout the renovation area.

Custom Cabinetry

The centerpiece of this renovation is a full suite of KraftMaid cabinetry in the Foxchase door style, built with all-plywood construction and soft-close hardware throughout. The design uses a two-tone finish that gives the kitchen real visual depth: upper cabinets and the island are finished in Wicker, while the base cabinets are finished in Muted Moss, a warm, muted green that grounds the space without overpowering it. 

A Rev-a-Shelf blind cabinet pullout was included to maximize corner storage. As with every Mountaineer project, the cabinetry is American-made and installed entirely in-house, from toe-kicks and trims to hardware and final adjustments.

Countertops and Plumbing Fixtures

Tyrol quartz was selected for the countertops, paired with a full-height backsplash in the same material for a clean, continuous look from counter to upper cabinet. The edge profile is a demi bullnose, adding a soft, classic detail to the surface. The sink is a stainless steel undermount with satin strainer baskets. A Moen 3/4 HP garbage disposal with an air switch rounds out the plumbing package. All countertops were templated using computerized laser systems and cut with CNC precision for tight seams and exact fits.

Lighting and Electrical

The electrical plan was designed to give this kitchen both strong task lighting and flexibility for accent fixtures:

      Eight LED recessed lights with dimmer capability throughout the kitchen
      Rough-in for pendant fixtures over the island
      Rough-in for undercabinet and above-cabinet lighting
      GFCI receptacles under the cabinets in the work area and in the island
      Dedicated circuits for all appliance locations
      Air-switched receptacle for the garbage disposal

All switches, receptacles, and cover plates were updated to white. Flush-mounted island and sink fixtures supplied by the homeowner were installed during final trim-out.

Paint and Trim

Paint-grade casing, base, and shoe molding were installed in the renovation area and matched to existing trim profiles throughout. Sherwin-Williams products were used for all painted surfaces: SuperPaint in satin on the walls, Masterhide flat white on the ceilings, and Masterhide semi-gloss white on all trim and doors. Painting covered the kitchen and living room in full, with the dining room ceiling also painted to tie the adjacent spaces together.

A Kitchen Designed for Everyday Living

The Petrasek kitchen renovation is a strong example of what thoughtful material selection and quality craftsmanship can do for a space. The two-tone KraftMaid cabinetry, Tyrol quartz countertops, and updated lighting come together to create a kitchen that feels both fresh and functional. Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths managed every aspect of this project in-house, and the result is a space built to serve their home for years to come.

A Bold Kitchen Renovation for the Jackson Family in Harpers Ferry, WV

Jul 14, 2026

The Jackson’s kitchen renovation in Harpers Ferry, WV is just one piece of an ongoing relationship with Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths. The goal was ambitious: tear out a dated kitchen, remove a wall to reshape the layout, and rebuild the space from the studs out with high-end cabinetry, quartz countertops, hardwood flooring, and a design built to function as well as it looks. The result is a complete reimagination of the main living area, carried out entirely by Mountaineer’s in-house team.

Layout and Structural Work

The most significant change was structural. The wall between the dining room and kitchen was removed and relocated approximately four feet toward the front of the house, opening the two spaces into a connected, open-plan layout. The load-bearing wall required support from two 11¾” LVL beams, with the new beam finished flush with the surrounding drywall. Mountaineer handled the engineering coordination, rough carpentry, and finished drywall as part of a single managed scope.

Custom Cabinetry

Cabinetry was specified for three rooms. The kitchen and laundry room received Woodhaven Shaker-style cabinets in Eagle Rock, while the powder room was fitted with the same Shaker style in Overcast. All cabinets feature full-overlay doors, all-plywood box construction, and soft-close hardware throughout. The two-finish approach gives each space its own character while keeping the overall palette cohesive. Mountaineer’s team handled the full installation in-house, including trims, toe-kicks, and all hardware.

Countertops and Plumbing Fixtures

Two quartz selections were specified for this renovation. The kitchen and laundry received Calacatta Arno with a full-height backsplash in the kitchen and a 4” backsplash in the laundry, both with a double-round edge profile. The powder room was fitted with Calacatta Laza, also with a 4” backsplash and a white rectangle bowl sink. All surfaces were templated with laser precision and cut using CNC technology for tight, clean seams. Plumbing fixtures throughout were specified in matte black, including a Moen Sinema pull-down faucet, a Moen Sip beverage faucet, and a Moen 3/4 HP disposal with a matte black air switch.

Lighting and Electrical

The electrical plan was built around both function and flexibility. Key elements include:

      Ten LED recessed lights throughout the kitchen and surrounding areas
      Rough-in for pendant fixtures over the island and undercabinet lighting
      Dedicated circuits for all appliance locations and a gas line rough-in for the new cooktop
      GFCI receptacles in the work area and island, plus a switched receptacle for the disposal

New venthood ducting and an exterior cap were installed to vent the gas cooktop. All switches, receptacles, and cover plates were updated to white, and flush-mounted fixtures supplied by the homeowner were installed during final trim-out.

Flooring, Paint, and Trim

New hardwood flooring was installed in the kitchen, powder room, and laundry room, then sanded and restained alongside the existing hardwood in adjoining spaces to create a single, continuous floor across the main level. Paint-grade casing, base, and shoe molding were installed to match existing profiles throughout. Sherwin-Williams SuperPaint was used on walls, Masterhide flat white on ceilings, and Masterhide semi-gloss white on all trim and doors. Painting extended into the living room, breakfast nook, and dining room, tying the newly opened floor plan together.

The Beginning of a Lasting Partnership

This renovation is exactly the kind of project that defines what Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths does best: a complex, multi-room transformation managed entirely in-house, from structural work to final punchout. With thoughtful material selections, precise craftsmanship, and a layout that now truly serves the way the home is lived in, this project sets a strong foundation for the work ahead. We look forward to continuing our partnership with the Jackson family and bringing the same level of care to every future project in their home.

A Complete Kitchen Transformation for the Wiggins Family in Falling Waters, WV

Jun 30, 2026

When the Wiggins family decided it was time to reimagine their main level, they came to Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths with a clear goal: a full kitchen overhaul that would improve both function and flow throughout the heart of their home. Located in Falling Waters, WV, this project went well beyond a standard kitchen update. From removing an existing pantry wall to opening up the entire main level with new flooring, trim, and cabinetry, the scope of work reflected a family ready for a complete refresh done right.

Opening Up the Space with Smart Structural Changes

One of the most impactful decisions in this renovation was removing the existing pantry walls and door to open up the layout. That space was converted into a pantry closet, keeping the storage functionality while eliminating the visual barrier that had been cutting off the kitchen from the rest of the main level. All beadboard, chair rail, and original baseboard and casing throughout the first floor were removed as well, setting the stage for a cleaner, more cohesive finish.

Interior doors to the new pantry closet, laundry room, and main-level bathroom were replaced with fresh paint-grade hollow core doors, bringing a unified look to the entire floor.

Custom KraftMaid Cabinetry Designed for Everyday Living

At the center of this kitchen transformation is a full suite of KraftMaid cabinetry, selected for its quality construction and lasting durability. As with all of Mountaineer’s projects, the cabinets are American-made and built to handle the demands of everyday life. The Wiggins’ design pairs two finishes for a layered, intentional look:

      Base cabinets in Shortbread with Maple construction and the Lyndale full-overlay door style
      Wall cabinets in Warm White using Evercore construction
      All-plywood box construction with soft-close hardware throughout
      Hardware in Verona Bronze, adding warmth and contrast to the two-tone cabinet palette

Four pantry closet shelves were also built and finished to match, keeping the new storage space consistent with the rest of the kitchen design. Mountaineer’s in-house team handled every aspect of the cabinet installation, from trimwork and toe-kicks to door adjustments and hardware placement.

Misterio Gold Quartz Countertops and Full-Height Backsplash

The countertop selection brings a striking focal point to the kitchen. The Wiggins family chose Misterio Gold quartz, a rich, movement-filled surface that plays beautifully against the warm Shortbread base cabinets. A full-height backsplash in the same material creates a bold, finished look that ties the cabinetry wall together from countertop to upper cabinet.

Mountaineer uses computerized laser templating and CNC-precision manufacturing to ensure each cut is exact and every seam is as tight and clean as possible. The result is countertops that look custom because they are. Plumbing fixtures were updated to match, including a Moen Weymouth faucet in oil rubbed bronze with a two-handle, high-arc, pull-down spray head, and a new Moen garbage disposal.

Lighting, Electrical, and the New Coffee Bar

This kitchen was rewired with intentional lighting in mind. The electrical plan included:

      Four LED recessed lights in the kitchen for clean, even overhead illumination
      Three pendant lights rough-in over the island, with the pendants selected by the homeowners
      Dedicated circuits for all appliance locations
      GFCI receptacles in the work area and island as required
      A dedicated receptacle at the new coffee bar station
      A switched receptacle for the garbage disposal

New venthood ducting and an exterior cap were installed for proper kitchen ventilation. All switches, receptacles, and cover plates were updated to white and placed to match the updated design. Mountaineer also installed the dishwasher and above-range microwave as part of the project scope.

New LVP Flooring Throughout the Entire Main Level

The existing flooring throughout the main level was removed and replaced with Mannington Realta SPC in Scandinavian Oak Natural, a 7×48 plank format that brings a clean, airy feel to the space. The installation covers the living room, dining room, kitchen, bathroom, closets, and laundry room, giving the entire main floor a single, continuous look.

The subfloor was prepared as needed before installation, and no shoe mold or quarter round was added, keeping the transition between flooring and trim clean and modern.

Fresh Paint, New Trim, and Finished Drywall

New paint-grade casing and baseboard were installed throughout the entire main level, replacing everything that was removed during demo. Mountaineer’s team finished all new drywall to Level 4 standards, patched and primed throughout, and painted walls, ceilings, and trim using Sherwin-Williams products:

      Walls: Sherwin-Williams SuperPaint in a satin sheen
      Ceilings: Sherwin-Williams Masterhide in flat white
      Trim and doors: Sherwin-Williams Masterhide in semi-gloss white

The result is a crisp, bright finish that lets the cabinetry and countertops do the talking throughout the space.

A Kitchen Designed for Everyday Living

From the structural changes that opened up the layout to the carefully selected materials that carry through every surface, the Wiggins kitchen renovation is a study in thoughtful design and quality craftsmanship. Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths managed every piece of this project in-house, from the first demo day to the final punchout, with no outsourcing and no shortcuts. The result is a main level that feels entirely new and built to last for years to come.

Before You Pick Your Cabinet Finish, Think About These 4 Things

Jun 10, 2026

Choosing a cabinet finish feels like it should be the fun part. But too many homeowners have experienced that sinking “that’s not what I picked” moment when the cabinets go up and the color looks nothing like it did in the showroom.

Cabinet finishes are more reactive than most people realize. Lighting shifts them. Undertones clash with them. Daily life tests them. There are four factors that make all the difference between a finish you’ll love for decades and one you’ll second-guess from day one.

What Lighting Will Your Cabinets Actually See?

This is the one most people skip, and the one that causes the most regret.

A cabinet finish doesn’t exist in a vacuum. It exists in your home, under your light bulbs, next to your windows. Natural light, warm incandescent, and soft white LED all interact with finishes differently. A finish that looks clean and creamy in the showroom can read yellow, green, or gray in a different space.

Always compare your samples in morning, afternoon, and evening lighting, and in multiple rooms. Walk the sample through the kitchen, hold it near a window, check it again at night with the overheads on. A finish that looks right in all three conditions is a finish you can trust.

What Are the Undertones in the Rest of the Space?

Undertones either harmonize or fight. When they fight, something feels off even if you can’t name exactly why.

Every material in your kitchen or bath carries an undertone. Countertops, backsplash, flooring, and paint all fall somewhere on the spectrum of warm, cool, beige, or grey. When your cabinet finish carries a different undertone than the elements around it, the whole space can feel unresolved no matter how beautiful each piece is individually.

Take stock of the dominant undertone in your existing or planned materials before committing. Warm wood floors pair naturally with warm-toned finishes. Cool grey quartz plays better with finishes that lean neutral or cool. When the undertones align, the room feels cohesive and complete.

What Level of Maintenance Do You Want to Commit To?

Every finish has a maintenance personality, and it’s worth being honest about your daily routine before you fall in love with a look.

Gloss finishes show fingerprints. Matte finishes show smudges. Dark stains show everything. That dramatic walnut or espresso finish photographs beautifully, but in a busy kitchen it will ask something of you every day. A family with heavy kitchen use is often better served by a mid-tone finish that hides the evidence of real life. A low-traffic guest bath is exactly the right place to indulge something more dramatic.

The goal is a finish that fits the life you actually live.

How Much Texture Do You Want to See?

Finish isn’t just about color. It’s about surface feel and visual texture, and those qualities read very differently once installed across a full run of cabinetry.

Natural wood finishes show grain variation, and that variation is part of what makes them beautiful. The grain gives each door its own character and fills a space with warmth that painted finishes can’t replicate. But if you find visual variation busy or distracting, a heavy wood stain may not be the right fit. Painted finishes and lighter stains let the wood recede and keep the eye moving smoothly across the space.

If you love the organic quality of natural wood, lean into it fully. Just know that no two doors will be identical, and that’s a feature, not a flaw.

Putting It All Together

Once you’ve worked through lighting, undertones, maintenance, and texture, put your sample to the real test. Bring it into your actual space, not the showroom. Hold it next to your countertops, flooring, and walls. Move around the room. Check it in the morning, the afternoon, and after the sun goes down. A finish that holds up across all of those conditions is one you can commit to with confidence.

From Entry Level to Owner: How Ben DeOms Built His Future at Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths

May 15, 2026

There’s a certain kind of person who shows up at 16 and never really leaves; not because they had nowhere else to go, but because they found something worth staying for. Ben DeOms is that person, and Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths is that place.

What began as a summer job during high school quietly became something much larger: a career, a calling, and eventually, ownership of one of the region’s most respected custom cabinetry and kitchen design companies. Ben’s story isn’t a corporate ascent or an overnight success. It’s the story of a young man who fell in love with the craft.

Starting at the Bottom, Learning Everything

Ben was still in high school when he first walked through the doors at MKB — working summers, evenings, and weekends while his classmates were clocking out. Most teenagers would have moved on. Ben moved up.

“I started here when I was 16 working summers, evenings and weekends during high school,” he recalls, “and then it just kind of grew from there. I learned a lot and eventually took over the business.”

That trajectory didn’t happen by accident. It happened because Ben paid attention. He absorbed the standards that had been set long before him, watched skilled craftsmen work, and internalized what it means to do a job right.

A Legacy Built on Quality and American-Made Materials

MKB has been serving the community for over 31 years. That kind of longevity doesn’t happen by cutting corners. Every project the team takes on is built with American-made materials and the kind of hands-on craftsmanship that’s increasingly rare in a world of flat-pack furniture and factory shortcuts.

The emphasis on quality isn’t just marketing language at MKB; it’s the foundation the company was built on, and it’s something Ben takes seriously as its new steward.

“Something that the previous owners of Mountaineer Kitchens and Baths did that I want to continue to emphasize throughout every job that we do is just the quality of work and the integrity of work that we do,” Ben says. “We’ve been around for over 31 years now and we continue to serve the community each and every day by the quality of work that we put out.”

That commitment runs through every cabinet door, every countertop, every custom detail, all of which are proudly sourced and crafted in America, installed by a team that takes pride in the result.

What Gets Him Out of Bed

Ask Ben what keeps him motivated, and he’ll give you two answers: the people he works alongside, and the look on a client’s face when they see their finished space for the first time.

“The part of the job that still gets me up in the morning is definitely the people I work with,” he says. “I really enjoy working with the people I do, and I’ve worked around most of them for five, ten, or even more years.”

That kind of team continuity is rare and it shows in the work. When craftsmen have been working together for a decade, they develop a shared language, a shared standard. There’s no need to explain what “good enough” isn’t.

And then there’s the client side:

“I also really enjoy seeing the transformation and the joy it brings to our clients and customers when they see the start-to-finish process — and that they really get to enjoy the finished space in their homes.”

That transformation, from empty walls and outdated cabinetry to a magazine-worthy kitchen, is the product MKB actually sells. Everything else is just the means to get there.

The Next Chapter: Showpieces and Expansion

Ben isn’t content to simply maintain what was built before him. With ownership has come vision and he’s thinking big.

“I think I’m most excited about the next chapter for Mountaineer Kitchens and Baths is the growth and the higher-end projects that we’re beginning to do more and more of — that are more showpiece quality and something you kind of see in a magazine,” he says. “That definitely excites me.”

The company recently opened a new showroom, giving clients a tangible look at what’s possible, highlighting spaces that reflect the full range of MKB’s craftsmanship. And Ben has his sights set further still: “moving to newer locations, our new showroom now, and expanding from there to eventually — hopefully — multiple locations.”

What Kept Him

It would be easy to assume that a young person stays at a company because it’s familiar, or comfortable, or simply the path of least resistance. But Ben’s loyalty to MKB was never passive.

“I think the thing that kept me a Mountaineer for as long as I’ve been here — and then turned into ownership eventually — was just the quality of work and what we do for people in their homes and serving the community.”

That’s the heart of it. A kid who showed up at 16 and found something that mattered — work done right, with materials built to last, by a team that genuinely cares. He grew into the role because the role was worth growing into.

Now, as owner, Ben DeOms carries that same standard forward.

One American-made cabinet, one transformed home, one proud client at a time.

A Bold and Functional Bathroom Renovation for the Dagg Family in Charles Town, WV

Apr 22, 2026

After completing a stunning kitchen renovation with Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths, the Dagg family returned to continue updating their home.  This time they focused on their bathroom. With a vision for a more modern, functional, and comfortable space, this project involved a full transformation from top to bottom.

By combining smart layout changes, high-quality materials, and detailed craftsmanship, the result is a bathroom that feels both elevated and tailored to everyday living.

Reworking the Layout for Better Flow and Function

This renovation began with a complete demolition of the existing bathroom, including the tub, shower, vanity, flooring, fixtures, and outdated finishes. The Mountaineer team then reimagined the space to improve both functionality and comfort.

Key structural updates included:

Framing a new closet and knee wall to better define the vanity area
Expanding the shower footprint by reframing existing walls
Adding a custom drywall niche for convenience and storage
Installing a new window to bring in natural light

These changes helped open up the space while creating a more intentional and efficient layout.

A Custom Tile Shower Built for Comfort

The new shower is a standout feature in this renovation, designed to provide both style and everyday usability.

Shower highlights include:

A fully waterproof Schluter shower system with Kerdi membrane
Matte black 4×16 vertical tile for a clean, modern look
2×2 mosaic tile flooring for added texture and grip
Dual niches with a granite shelf for practical storage
Built-in bench seating for comfort
Polished brass Schluter edging for a refined finish

Paired with a frameless glass shower door and brushed gold fixtures, the shower creates a bold and sophisticated focal point.

Heated Floors and Thoughtful Tile Design

To enhance comfort, the Dagg family chose to include Schluter Ditra-Heat flooring throughout the bathroom.

Flooring features include:

12×24 tile in a clean brick pattern
Integrated heating system for year-round comfort
Coordinated grout and polished brass transitions for a cohesive finish

This combination not only improves comfort but also adds a high-end feel to the entire space.

Custom Vanity and High-End Finishes

The vanity area was designed to balance functionality with a modern aesthetic.

Key features include:

KraftMaid vanity cabinetry with all-plywood construction and soft-close hardware
Hickory cabinetry finished in Shortbread for warmth and character
Granite countertops in Grey Nuevo, extending to the shower bench, curb, and niche shelf
Dual vessel sinks for a distinctive, modern look
Dedicated outlets within cabinetry and at the vanity for convenience

This space also includes a dedicated makeup area, adding both usability and personalization to the design.

Smart Technology and Upgraded Plumbing Features

This bathroom renovation also incorporated several thoughtful upgrades to enhance daily living:

A Moen electronic cleansing bidet toilet for added comfort and hygiene
Brushed gold Moen fixtures, including vessel faucets and shower controls
Dual body sprays and a handheld shower option for a customizable experience

These features reflect the Daggs’ focus on blending comfort, convenience, and modern design.

Lighting, Electrical, and Finishing Touches

Lighting and electrical upgrades played a key role in completing the space:

Three recessed LED lights for general illumination
Sconce vanity lighting for focused task lighting
Two fan/light combo units for proper ventilation
Heated floor thermostat and dedicated electrical connections

The space was finished with fresh paint throughout, matching trim details, and carefully installed hardware and accessories to bring everything together seamlessly.

Continuing the Transformation of the Dagg Home

This bathroom renovation is a perfect example of how Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths helps homeowners continue improving their spaces over time. After successfully completing their kitchen project, the Daggs trusted the team once again to deliver a bathroom that reflects their style and meets their needs.

From layout changes to material selections and final installation, every step of the project was handled with attention to detail and a commitment to quality craftsmanship.

Preparing for a Bathroom Remodel: A Step-by-Step Guide for Homeowners

Apr 3, 2026

Planning a bathroom renovation can feel overwhelming at first, but with the right approach, it becomes an exciting process that leads to a space you’ll enjoy every day. Whether you’re updating an outdated layout or creating something completely new, preparation is key to a smooth and successful project.

At Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths, we guide homeowners throughout the Eastern Panhandle through every stage—from design to installation—with a fully in-house team and high-quality, American-made materials.

Below is a simple, practical guide to help you prepare for your bathroom remodel.

Create a List of Needs and Wants

Before diving into design selections, it’s important to clearly define what you need versus what you want.

Identify Your Daily Needs

Start by thinking about how you currently use your bathroom:

Do you need more storage?
Is your current layout functional?
Are there accessibility concerns now or in the future?
Build Your Wish List

Once the essentials are covered, consider upgrades that would enhance your space:

Larger shower or freestanding tub
Double vanity
Heated flooring
Updated lighting or mirrors

Having both lists prepared helps guide design decisions and keeps your project focused.

Create a Realistic Budget

A well-planned budget sets the foundation for a successful renovation.

Understand What Impacts Cost

Bathroom remodel costs can vary depending on:

Size and layout changes
Material selections (tile, cabinetry, fixtures)
Plumbing and electrical updates
Custom features like niches, benches, or heated floors
Plan for Flexibility

It’s always wise to allow room in your budget for:

Design upgrades you may fall in love with
Unexpected conditions behind walls or under flooring

At Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths, we walk you through material options and design choices that align with your budget without sacrificing quality.

Contact Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths

One of the most important steps is choosing the right team.

Why Work with Mountaineer?
All work is handled in-house from start to finish
We use high-quality, American-made cabinetry and materials
You’ll have a dedicated team guiding your project every step of the way
What to Expect During Your Consultation
A discussion of your goals, needs, and inspiration
Review of layout possibilities and design direction
Guidance on materials, finishes, and features
A clear outline of next steps in the process

Starting with an experienced team helps eliminate guesswork and keeps your project moving smoothly.

Decide on Temporary Bathroom Arrangements

During a bathroom remodel, access to your space will be limited or unavailable.

Plan Ahead for Daily Use

Consider:

Using another bathroom in your home
Coordinating schedules with family members
Making temporary adjustments to your daily routine
Think About Project Timeline

Your remodeling team will provide a timeline, allowing you to plan accordingly and minimize disruption.  Preparing ahead of time helps reduce stress once construction begins.

Clean the Area and Remove All Items

Before work starts, clearing out the space is essential.

What to Remove
Personal items and toiletries
Towels, rugs, and décor
Items stored in cabinets and drawers
Why It Matters
Protects your belongings from dust and damage
Allows the team to begin work immediately
Keeps the project on schedule

Taking the time to properly prepare the space ensures a smoother start to your renovation.

Enjoy Your New Bathroom

Once the work is complete, you’ll be able to enjoy a space designed specifically for your lifestyle.

What You Can Expect
Improved functionality and layout
High-quality materials built to last
A fresh, updated look that fits your home

At Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths, our goal is to deliver a finished product that reflects your vision while providing long-term value and comfort.

Ready to Start Your Bathroom Remodel?

Preparing for a bathroom remodel doesn’t have to be complicated. With the right planning and the right team, the process can be smooth, organized, and even enjoyable.

A Fresh, Modern Kitchen Renovation for the Dagg Family in Charles Town, WV

Mar 16, 2026

When the Dagg family in Charles Town decided it was time to update their kitchen, they were looking for a space that felt brighter, more functional, and better suited for everyday living. With a thoughtful redesign, upgraded finishes, and improved lighting, the Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths team helped transform their kitchen into a welcoming centerpiece of the home.

This renovation combined structural improvements, custom cabinetry, and carefully selected materials to create a kitchen that balances style, efficiency, and durability.

Preparing the Space for a Complete Kitchen Transformation

The project began with a full demolition of the existing kitchen elements to prepare for the new layout and finishes. Our team removed the original cabinetry, countertops, sink, faucet, garbage disposal, flooring, and tile throughout the kitchen. Bulkheads above the wall cabinets were also removed to allow for a cleaner, more open cabinet design.

A new replacement window was installed above the sink, bringing additional natural light into the kitchen and helping create a brighter workspace.

As with every Mountaineer project, the space was carefully prepared for the next phase of construction, including drywall repairs and updates finished to meet drywall standards for a smooth, professional finish.

Custom Cabinetry Designed for Style and Function

At the heart of this kitchen renovation is a beautiful set of KraftMaid cabinets, designed to deliver both durability and visual appeal.

The Daggs selected:

Door Style: Lyndale
Overlay: Full
Construction: All-plywood construction with soft-close hardware
Wood Species: Evercore
Finish: Harbor

The cabinetry layout was designed to maximize storage and usability, while maintaining a clean and modern look. Our team handled the full installation process, including all trim work, toe kicks, door adjustments, and hardware placement to ensure every detail aligned perfectly with the design.

Elegant Quartz Countertops and Stylish Finishes

To complement the cabinetry, the Daggs selected Cambria Portrush quartz countertops, a durable and visually striking surface that brings both elegance and practicality to the kitchen.

Features included:

Ogee edge profile for added character
Stainless steel sink supplied and installed by Mountaineer
Professional templating and fabrication using advanced digital measuring technology for precise installation

The countertops were paired with a Pamarva SOHO 2×5 picket tile backsplash in Canvas White, installed in a classic pattern and finished with Frosty grout and matte white Schluter edging. This combination adds texture and visual interest without overwhelming the space.

Lighting, Electrical, and Functional Upgrades

Lighting played a key role in enhancing both the functionality and atmosphere of the new kitchen.

Electrical improvements included:

Six recessed LED ceiling lights for even illumination
Four pendant lights above the island
One pendant light over the sink
Dedicated circuits for appliances
GFCI outlets in work areas and island
Specialty outlets inside cabinets for appliances and water systems

These upgrades ensure the kitchen is as practical as it is beautiful.

Flooring and Finishing Touches

To tie the space together, new flooring was installed throughout the kitchen, living room, and laundry room areas.

The Daggs chose Mannington Adura Max click-lock LVT flooring in Vienna Alabaster, offering the warmth of wood with the durability and moisture resistance needed for busy households.

Additional finishing details included:

Paint-grade casing, base, and shoe molding to match the home’s existing trim
Fresh paint throughout the renovated areas using Sherwin-Williams finishes
Careful installation of plumbing fixtures including a Hotis brushed gold farmhouse apron sink, Moen Cia faucet, and Moen garbage disposal

Every detail—from lighting placement to cabinet hardware—was installed by the Mountaineer team to ensure a cohesive and high-quality result.

A Kitchen Designed for Everyday Living

The completed kitchen renovation for the Dagg family showcases how thoughtful design and quality craftsmanship can transform a home’s most-used space. With upgraded lighting, modern cabinetry, beautiful quartz countertops, and durable flooring, this kitchen now offers both the style and functionality the family was looking for.

Projects like this highlight Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths’ commitment to delivering renovations that not only look beautiful but are built to last.
